head:
sincere, genuine, without hypocrisy; of good character, lacking pretense and prideful show 
unfeigned, real, sincere, without hypocrisy Rom. 12:9

hypocrisy (an extension of an actor in a play, not found in the NT), implying arrogance and hardness of heart, utterly devoid of sincerity and genuineness 
a response, answer; an over-acting personification, acting; hypocrisy, simulation, Mt. 23:28; Mk. 12:15; Lk. 12:1; Gal. 2:13; 1Tim. 4:2; 1Pet. 2:1*

1) flattery, slipperiness, fine promises, smoothness
1a) slipperiness
1b) fine promises

to join in one’s hypocrisy be hypocritical 
to dissemble, feign with, or in the same manner as another, join in the playing of the hypocrite, Gal. 2:13*
